evidence.reference_title: Ataxia and hypogonadism caused by the loss of ubiquitin ligase activity of the U box protein CHIP.
evidence.snippet: Introduction of the Thr246Met mutation into CHIP results in a loss of ubiquitin ligase activity measured directly using recombinant proteins as well as in cell culture models.
evidence.explanation: Introducing the index SCAR16 variant into CHIP abolishes ligase activity in recombinant protein and in cells, which is a direct variant-to-enzyme-defect causal claim.

evidence.reference_title: A novel STUB1 p.(Gln118*) nonsense variant in compound heterozygosity causes autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia type 16 in a Chinese patient.
evidence.snippet: We found that STUB1 p.(Gln118*) variant generated truncated proteins of the C-terminus of Hsc70-interacting protein and caused the loss function of ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence.explanation: A nonsense allele reaches the same endpoint by truncation, showing the edge holds across variant classes and not only for the index missense allele.

context.support_span: We discovered a genetic disease, now known as spinocerebellar autosomal recessive 16 (SCAR16), resulting from a coding mutation that caused a loss of CHIP ubiquitin ligase function.
The initial mutation describing SCAR16 was a missense mutation in the ubiquitin ligase domain of CHIP (p.T246M).

Using multiple biophysical and cellular approaches, we demonstrated that T246M mutation results in structural disorganization and misfolding of the CHIP U-box domain, promoting oligomerization, and increased proteasome-dependent turnover.
CHIP-T246M has no ligase activity, but maintains interactions with chaperones and chaperone-related functions.
